overview:

This is one of our **Weekend Getaways**, built for a quick mountain reset without burning your leave. The full day-by-day plan for this trip is still being finalised, so please check with our team for the latest itinerary and inclusions before you book. What we can promise is the Travel Devils way of doing things: good company, a relaxed pace and a trip that feels easy from start to finish.

overview:
Need a quick mountain fix? This 1 Night / 2 Days weekend getaway takes you to Kanatal, a small village and hill station in Uttarakhand, and pairs it with a fun-filled day at Tehri Lake. Kanatal sits on the Chamba-Mussoorie road, about 78 km from Dehradun, 38 km from Mussoorie, 18 km from Chamba and nearly 300 km from Delhi, so it's close enough for a weekend and far enough to feel like a proper escape.

Day 1 is all about adventure at the campsite, with **Zip Line, Burma Bridge and Sky Cycling** included, plus a visit to the Surkanda Devi Temple. You spend the night at a Kanatal campsite with evening snacks and dinner. Day 2 takes you to **Tehri Lake** for water sports before heading back. Other highlights on this trip include the Eco Park and the Giant Swing.

You travel by AC bus or Traveller, with a trip coordinator along for the ride and 24x7 customer support, so all you need to do is pack a bag and show up.

faqs.q: How long is the Kanatal Tehri trip?
faqs.a: It's a 1 Night / 2 Days weekend trip, with one night's stay at a campsite in Kanatal.

faqs.q: What's included in the trip?
faqs.a: Travel by AC bus or Traveller, 1 night at a Kanatal campsite, meals (2 breakfasts, 1 dinner and 1 evening snacks), a Tehri Lake visit for water sports, adventure activities (Zip Line, Burma Bridge, Sky Cycling), a trip coordinator and 24x7 customer support.

faqs.q: What's not included?
faqs.a: 5% GST, extra drinks, food, tea and snacks, tickets for any sightseeing or extra activity outside the camp area, travel insurance, medical expenses beyond first aid, and personal expenses like tips, laundry, mineral water and camera fees. Any extra cost from landslides, road closures or other unforeseen events is also not included.

faqs.a: It starts from ₹4,999 per person on Quad Sharing. Triple Sharing is ₹5,199 and Dual Sharing is ₹5,399, with 5% GST extra.

faqs.a: Kanatal is nearly 300 km from Delhi. It sits on the Chamba-Mussoorie road, about 78 km from Dehradun and 38 km from Mussoorie.

overview:
Kashmir is every bit as beautiful as the photos, and this backpacking trip makes it easy to see the best of it. Over 5 Nights / 6 Days of stay, you cover the valley's big four: **Srinagar, Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam**, with breathtaking landscapes, a unique culture and plenty of room for adventure.

Your journey begins with a sleeper AC bus from Delhi to Jammu, then onward to Srinagar. From there, you head out on day trips to Gulmarg and Sonamarg, then to Pahalgam for sightseeing of **Aru Valley, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari**, which is included. Back in Srinagar, it's local sightseeing, a 1-hour **Shikara ride** and a night on a **houseboat**, before you travel back via Jammu to Delhi.

All sightseeing is by Tempo Traveller or cab depending on group size, with a tour leader throughout. You get 5 nights of accommodation on double or triple sharing and 10 meals (5 breakfasts and 5 dinners). Kashmir can be enjoyed in any season depending on what you want to do, so pick your vibe and come along.

faqs.q: How long is the Kashmir trip?
faqs.a: The trip is listed as 5 Nights / 6 Days with 5 nights of accommodation, plus sleeper AC bus transfers from Delhi to Jammu and back.

faqs.q: Which places does the trip cover?
faqs.a: Srinagar, Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam, including sightseeing of Aru Valley, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari, Srinagar local sightseeing, a 1-hour Shikara ride and a houseboat stay in Srinagar.

faqs.q: What's included?
faqs.a: Sleeper AC bus transfers Delhi to Jammu and back, all sightseeing by Tempo Traveller or cab depending on group size, 5 nights' accommodation on double or triple sharing, Aru Valley, Betaab Valley and Chandanwari sightseeing, 10 meals (5 breakfasts and 5 dinners), a 1-hour Shikara ride and a tour leader.

faqs.q: What's not included?
faqs.a: 5% GST, Srinagar airport pickup and drop, lunch, the Gulmarg Gondola ride (we'll help you book it), the Sonamarg Zero Point cab, snow-chained SUVs if needed, pony rides and other activities, and personal expenses like tips, monument entries and laundry. Costs from landslides or road blocks are borne by guests on the spot.

faqs.q: How much does the Kashmir trip cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹20,499 per person on Triple Sharing, and Dual Sharing is ₹22,499, with 5% GST extra.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start?
faqs.a: The trip starts with a sleeper AC bus from Delhi to Jammu. Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kashmir?
faqs.a: Kashmir can be visited in any season depending on what you want to do: winter brings snow to places like Gulmarg, while spring and summer are great for green valleys and sightseeing.

faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates. Many travellers join solo, and groups are usually 8 to 50 people.

overview:
This 6 Nights / 7 Days Leh to Leh trip is a splendid blend of adventure, serenity and culture, set against Ladakh's breathtaking scenery. You arrive in Leh, take a day to acclimatise, explore Leh on a local sightseeing day, then head out to **Nubra Valley**, **Turtuk** and **Pangong Lake** before the trip wraps up with a drop to Leh airport.

In Nubra you'll see Diskit Monastery and the Hunder sand dunes with their Bactrian camels. **Turtuk**, one of India's northernmost villages and formerly part of Pakistan, gives you a glimpse into Balti culture: lush green apricot fields, rustic wooden homes and friendly smiles, a striking contrast to Ladakh's arid mountains. Nearby, the Thang border viewpoint is another highlight.

Choose how you ride: a **sitting coach**, or a **Royal Enfield Himalayan** solo or with a pillion. The biking option includes bike rent for 5 days, fuel as per itinerary, riding gear, an RE mechanic with spares and a mechanical and luggage backup vehicle. Everyone gets 6 nights of stay across hotels, camps or cottages and homestays, all inner line permits, a complimentary bonfire night and a Team Captain throughout.

faqs.q: How long is the Leh to Leh trip?
faqs.a: It's a 6 Nights / 7 Days trip that starts with your arrival in Leh and ends with a drop to Leh airport.

faqs.q: Which places does the trip cover?
faqs.a: Leh local sightseeing, Nubra Valley (including Diskit Monastery and the Hunder sand dunes), Turtuk village and the Thang border viewpoint, and Pangong Lake.

faqs.q: What are the price options?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹18,999 per person in a Sitting Coach. On a Royal Enfield Himalayan it's ₹22,999 with a pillion and ₹27,999 as a solo rider, with 5% GST extra.

faqs.q: What's included?
faqs.a: 6 nights' stay in hotels, camps or cottages and homestays on double, triple or quad sharing, all meals mentioned in the itinerary, inner line permits, a backup vehicle, first aid kit, a complimentary bonfire night, a Team Captain, group pickup and drop, tolls and parking, and 24x7 customer support. The biking option adds bike rent for 5 days, fuel as per itinerary, riding gear and an RE mechanic with spare parts.

faqs.q: What's not included?
faqs.a: 5% GST, flights or rail fares, early hotel check-in, meals not listed in the inclusions, monument entry and parking fees during sightseeing, personal expenses, and extra costs from delays, flight cancellations, landslides or roadblocks. For bikers, spare parts for accidental damage, towing and servicing costs are also extra.

faqs.q: Do I need to acclimatise in Leh?
faqs.a: Yes. Leh sits at around 3,500 m, so the first day of the trip is kept for rest and acclimatisation, and it's wise to take it easy, stay hydrated and avoid exertion on arrival.

faqs.q: Is a double sharing room available?
faqs.a: Stays are on double, triple or quad sharing, and a double sharing room is available at an extra charge.

faqs.q: When does the trip depart, and can I join solo?
faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates. Many travellers join solo, and groups are usually 8 to 50 people.

overview:
Meghalaya, the "Abode of Clouds", is lush, misty and full of surprises, and this 5 Nights / 6 Days backpacking trip packs in the very best of it. The trip runs from Guwahati to Guwahati, starting with the scenic drive to Shillong via the gorgeous **Umiam Lake** (Barapani).

From Shillong you head to Cherrapunji via **Laitlum Canyon** and the Mawkdok Dympep viewpoint, with views of Nohkalikai Falls, the Garden of Caves, Arwah Caves and Seven Sisters Falls (if time permits). Then comes the big one: the trek to the famous **Double Decker Living Root Bridge** at Nongriat, with a trek guide included. After that you visit **Mawlynnong**, often called Asia's cleanest village, and spend a night at **Dawki**, known for its crystal-clear river, before returning via Shnongpdeng and Jowai to Shillong and finally a drop at Guwahati airport.

You stay 2 nights in Shillong, 2 in Cherrapunji and 1 in Dawki, with 5 breakfasts and a dinner in Dawki. All local transport by Tempo Traveller, SUV or sedan is covered, along with tolls, parking, fuel and driver allowance. September to December is the best time to go.

faqs.q: How long is the Meghalaya trip?
faqs.a: It's a 5 Nights / 6 Days trip: 2 nights in Shillong, 2 nights in Cherrapunji and 1 night in Dawki.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start and end?
faqs.a: The trip runs from Guwahati to Guwahati, ending with a drop at Guwahati airport. Pickup and drop are at fixed timings, and your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: What's included?
faqs.a: Pickup and drop at fixed timings, local sightseeing transport by Tempo Traveller, SUV or sedan from Guwahati to Guwahati, 5 nights' stay with 5 breakfasts and 1 dinner in Dawki, a Nongriat trek guide, all toll, parking, fuel and driver allowance, and an operations executive on call 24x7.

faqs.q: What's not included?
faqs.a: 5% GST, entry fees to sightseeing places, meals not listed in the inclusions, personal expenses like tips and laundry, any extra sightseeing or pickup and drop from other points, use of the vehicle at night, and any safari, boating or guide charges.

faqs.q: How much does the Meghalaya trip cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹20,499 per person on Triple Sharing, and Dual Sharing is ₹22,499, with 5% GST extra.

faqs.q: How tough is the Nongriat trek?
faqs.a: The trek to the Double Decker Root Bridge involves going down and back up thousands of steps, so a basic level of fitness and good walking shoes help a lot. A trek guide is included.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Meghalaya?
faqs.a: September to December is the best time to visit, when the landscapes are lush and the waterfalls are still flowing.

faqs.q: When does the trip depart, and can I join solo?
faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates. Many travellers join solo, and groups are usually 8 to 50 people.
